title: Julia Performance Tracking: database
description_html: Read-only SQL over the database behind perf.julialang.org: Julia CI timing, Nanosoldier benchmarks, PkgEval, TTFX, package downloads and Buildkite agents, refreshed every hour. Queries are limited to 2 seconds and 5000 rows; for more, download the whole database. The API serves what the site's pages show; llms.txt explains both. Times are UTC, durations seconds, benchmark times nanoseconds.

meta.description: Key-value settings: the schema version and the change sequences (change_seq, change_seq:<source>) the API uses as ETags.

source_runs.description: One row per fetcher run: when each source (timing, benchmarks, pkgeval, ttfx, packages, agents) ran and whether it succeeded. The freshness signal.

columns.ok: 1 when the run succeeded, 0 when it failed, NULL while running
columns.error: the error message of a failed run

commits.description: Reserved for commit metadata from a clone of JuliaLang/julia; not filled yet. Use builds for commit subjects and authors.

builds.description: Buildkite builds of Julia master. Pipelines: julia-ci (current), julia-master and julia-master-scheduled (stopped receiving builds in July 2026).

columns.commit_prefix: the first 8 characters of the commit SHA; every build has it
columns.commit_sha: the full SHA, on builds fetched from the Buildkite API (most older rows are NULL)
columns.message: the commit subject, cut at 80 characters
columns.created_at: when the build was created, UTC
columns.started_at: first job started; NULL on builds imported from before September 2026
columns.finished_at: last job finished; NULL like started_at

job_kinds.description: Classification of job names (kind, OS, triplet, flags). Reserved; not filled yet.

jobs.description: One row per job attempt of a build.

columns.name: the Buildkite step name, with emoji codes such as :linux:
columns.retry: attempt number within the build for that name, 0 first
columns.soft_failed: 1 when the job was allowed to fail
columns.runnable_at: when the job could start; runnable to started is its queue wait
columns.agent_hostname: the machine the job ran on

raw_builds.description: The Buildkite build JSON as fetched, zstd-compressed, kept because Buildkite only retains a window of builds.

coverage.description: Test coverage of a master commit from Codecov and Coveralls, in percent.

bench_reports.description: Nanosoldier benchmark reports. kind 'daily' reports run every few days on the master commit of that day and compare with an earlier daily report (the baseline).

columns.path: the report's directory under NanosoldierReports/benchmark, such as by_date/2026-09/13
columns.baseline_commit_sha: the commit it was compared with
columns.report_regressions: how many benchmarks Nanosoldier flagged as regressions

bench_names.description: Every benchmark: its BaseBenchmarks group (grp) and name.

columns.name: the benchmark's path within the group as BaseBenchmarks writes it, e.g. index/('sumelt', '1.0:1.0:100000.0')

bench_results.description: One row per report, benchmark and estimate. Large (millions of rows): filter on bench_id and stat, or use the snapshot.

columns.stat: the BenchmarkTools estimate: minimum, median, mean or std

bench_verdicts.description: Nanosoldier's comparison of each benchmark against the baseline report.

columns.time_ratio: this report's time over the baseline's; above 1 is slower
columns.time_tolerance: the ratio change Nanosoldier tolerates for this benchmark

bench_errors.description: Benchmarks that errored on a report, with the error.

bench_report_groups.description: Per report, group and estimate: the geometric mean over the group's benchmarks and how many there were, for each metric.

pkgeval_reports.description: PkgEval daily runs of the whole package ecosystem against Julia master, with the count of each outcome.

columns.path: the report's directory under NanosoldierReports/pkgeval, such as by_date/2026-09/09
columns.commit_sha: the Julia commit tested (8 characters on old reports)

pkgeval_reasons.description: Per report: how many packages had each status and failure reason.

packages.description: Package names that appear in PkgEval results. About 2.9k uuid-shaped names come from 2019-20 reports and can be ignored.

pkgeval_results.description: One row per report and package: whether its tests passed on that Julia commit. Large: filter by package_id or report_id.

columns.status: ok, fail, crash, skip or kill
columns.reason: why it did not pass, e.g. test_failures, precompile, time_limit

ttfx_jobs.description: The TTFX job of each julia-ci master build: it precompiles, loads and runs a set of package tasks (Julia-TTFX-Snippets) and records the times.

columns.build_created_at: when the build was created, UTC (minute precision)

ttfx_results.description: Per TTFX job and task: the minimum over the job's repeats, in seconds.

columns.load: the task script's load phase on its first run
columns.run: its run phase on the first run
columns.warm: the best total of the later runs
columns.load_gcoff: load, from repeats with the GC disabled

ttfx_failures.description: Tasks that failed in a TTFX job, with the error.

ttfx_arms.description: The Julia builds (arms) a TTFX job compared, with their commits.

ttfx_samples.description: Every record of a TTFX job's results file, in order, so other statistics than the minimum can be recomputed.

ttfx_prs.description: The latest finished TTFX comparison of every open julia pull request that has one: the head against the master build of the merge-base, as the julia-pr TTFX job judged it. Current state only; a closed pull request's row is deleted.

columns.pr_head_sha: the pull request's head now; differs from head_commit when it has moved on since the job
columns.n_improvements: robust improvements, per task and metric plus suite metrics
columns.n_regressions: robust regressions, counted the same way
columns.suite: JSON: per metric, the geometric mean over tasks of head/base per block, the verdict and the task count
columns.tasks: JSON: the tasks with a robust improvement or regression, their ratios and notes
columns.ci_commit: the pull request head the CI columns were looked up for
columns.ci_build: the newest julia-pr build of ci_commit, NULL when it has none
columns.ci_state: that build's Buildkite state (passed, failed, failing, running, ...), or none when the commit has no build

raw_ttfx.description: The TTFX job's result files as fetched, zstd-compressed.

dl_resource_types.description: Package server requests per day by resource type, status and client type, as published by julialang-logs.

dl_julia_versions.description: Package server requests per day by the requesting Julia version.

dl_julia_systems.description: Package server requests per day by the requesting platform.

dl_client_types.description: Package server requests per day by client type (user, ci, ...).

dl_package_uuids.description: Package UUIDs seen in download rows; join registry_packages on uuid for names.

registry_packages.description: The General registry's packages: uuid, name and path, refreshed every ingest.

dl_packages.description: Successful requests per day, package and client type. The only history there is: upstream keeps 3 days.

columns.request_addrs: distinct addresses within this row only; never sum across rows

dl_series.description: Total, user and CI package requests per day, as the Downloads page draws them.

dl_mix.description: Requests per day by Julia minor version (kind='version', key like 1.12) or release stage (kind='stage', key stable, rc, beta, alpha, other); key '*' is the day's total.

julia_tags.description: Julia releases from GitHub, for marking release dates on charts.

agent_snapshots.description: When the Buildkite agents were listed (every ingest).

agent_snapshot_members.description: Which agents were connected at each snapshot.

agents.description: Every Buildkite agent seen: host, queue, OS, state, first and last seen, and its current job.

columns.fold_key: the name without its '.N' slot suffix, to group per-job agents by host
columns.job_json: the running job as JSON, when connected

source_freshness.title: When each source last ran
source_freshness.sql:
SELECT source, max(finished_at) AS last_ok
FROM source_runs WHERE ok = 1 GROUP BY source ORDER BY source

latest_build_slowest_jobs.title: Slowest jobs of the latest julia-ci build
latest_build_slowest_jobs.sql:
SELECT j.name, round(j.duration_s / 60, 1) AS minutes, j.state, j.agent_hostname
FROM jobs j JOIN builds b ON b.id = j.build_id
WHERE b.pipeline = 'julia-ci' AND b.number = (SELECT max(number) FROM builds WHERE pipeline = 'julia-ci')
ORDER BY j.duration_s DESC LIMIT 20

job_duration_by_week.title: One job's duration by week
job_duration_by_week.description: Weekly mean and count of passing runs of a job on julia-ci over the last :days days; job is its exact name, e.g. :linux: test x86_64-linux-gnu
job_duration_by_week.sql:
SELECT strftime('%Y-%W', b.created_at) AS week, count(*) AS runs, round(avg(j.duration_s) / 60, 1) AS mean_minutes
FROM jobs j JOIN builds b ON b.id = j.build_id
WHERE j.name = :job AND b.pipeline = 'julia-ci' AND j.state = 'passed' AND b.created_at >= date('now', '-' || :days || ' days')
GROUP BY week ORDER BY week

queue_wait_by_build.title: Queue wait per julia-ci build over the last :days days
queue_wait_by_build.sql:
SELECT b.number, b.commit_prefix, count(*) AS jobs,
  round(avg((julianday(j.started_at) - julianday(j.runnable_at)) * 86400)) AS mean_wait_s,
  round(max((julianday(j.started_at) - julianday(j.runnable_at)) * 86400)) AS max_wait_s
FROM jobs j JOIN builds b ON b.id = j.build_id
WHERE b.pipeline = 'julia-ci' AND j.runnable_at IS NOT NULL AND b.created_at >= date('now', '-' || :days || ' days')
GROUP BY b.id ORDER BY b.number DESC

latest_benchmark_regressions.title: Regressions in the latest Nanosoldier daily report
latest_benchmark_regressions.sql:
SELECT n.grp, n.name, round(v.time_ratio, 2) AS time_ratio, round(v.memory_ratio, 2) AS memory_ratio
FROM bench_verdicts v JOIN bench_names n ON n.id = v.bench_id
WHERE v.verdict = 'regression' AND v.report_id = (SELECT id FROM bench_reports WHERE kind = 'daily' ORDER BY date DESC LIMIT 1)
ORDER BY v.time_ratio DESC LIMIT 100

benchmark_history.title: One benchmark's minimum time over time
benchmark_history.description: grp is the group (e.g. array); name is the exact benchmark name from bench_names
benchmark_history.sql:
SELECT r.date, r.commit_sha, res.time_ns, res.memory_bytes, res.allocs
FROM bench_results res JOIN bench_names n ON n.id = res.bench_id JOIN bench_reports r ON r.id = res.report_id
WHERE n.grp = :grp AND n.name = :name AND res.stat = 'minimum' AND r.kind = 'daily'
ORDER BY r.date DESC LIMIT 200

package_pkgeval_history.title: A package's PkgEval history
package_pkgeval_history.sql:
SELECT r.date, p.status, p.reason, p.version, r.julia_version
FROM pkgeval_results p JOIN packages k ON k.id = p.package_id JOIN pkgeval_reports r ON r.id = p.report_id
WHERE k.name = :package AND r.kind = 'daily' ORDER BY r.date DESC LIMIT 100

pkgeval_newly_broken.title: Packages that passed the previous PkgEval report and not the latest
pkgeval_newly_broken.sql:
WITH latest AS (SELECT r.id, r.date FROM pkgeval_reports r WHERE r.kind = 'daily' AND EXISTS (SELECT 1 FROM pkgeval_results x WHERE x.report_id = r.id) ORDER BY r.date DESC LIMIT 2)
SELECT k.name, new.status, new.reason
FROM pkgeval_results new JOIN pkgeval_results old ON old.package_id = new.package_id JOIN packages k ON k.id = new.package_id
WHERE new.report_id = (SELECT id FROM latest ORDER BY date DESC LIMIT 1)
  AND old.report_id = (SELECT id FROM latest ORDER BY date ASC LIMIT 1)
  AND old.status = 'ok' AND new.status != 'ok' ORDER BY k.name

ttfx_task_history.title: TTFX of one task per master build over the last :days days
ttfx_task_history.description: task is Package/Snippet as in ttfx_results.task, e.g. BaseDirs/Project-Path
ttfx_task_history.sql:
SELECT j.build, substr(j.commit_sha, 1, 10) AS commit_sha, j.build_created_at, r.precompile, r.load, r.run, r.warm, r.load_gcoff, r.run_gcoff, r.warm_gcoff
FROM ttfx_results r JOIN ttfx_jobs j ON j.job_uuid = r.job_uuid
WHERE r.task = :task AND j.build_created_at >= date('now', '-' || :days || ' days')
ORDER BY j.build_created_at

package_downloads_by_day.title: One package's downloads per day, user and CI
package_downloads_by_day.sql:
SELECT d.date, sum(CASE WHEN d.client_type = 'user' THEN d.request_count ELSE 0 END) AS user,
  sum(CASE WHEN d.client_type = 'ci' THEN d.request_count ELSE 0 END) AS ci
FROM dl_packages d JOIN dl_package_uuids u ON u.id = d.package_id JOIN registry_packages g ON g.uuid = u.uuid
WHERE g.name = :package GROUP BY d.date ORDER BY d.date

connected_agents.title: Buildkite agents connected at the latest listing, with their jobs
connected_agents.sql:
SELECT name, queue, os, arch, last_seen, json_extract(job_json, '$.name') AS job
FROM agents WHERE state = 'connected' ORDER BY queue, name
